options.text: Whether an inside pass is now usable
Whether staying at the boards is always required
Whether F2’s earlier position still guarantees an outlet

before.explanation: Pressure can change the outlet. A pass still depends on control and a clear actual lane.

after.prompt: To begin giving the puck more room from D1, which short carry could YOU explore in this view?

options.text: A small move toward the nearby side boards
A small move toward the middle of the rink

after.explanation: D1 is on the middle side. A small move toward the boards initially increases the puck’s separation from D1; moving inward initially brings it closer. Keep the puck controlled and leave room to move: this is not an instruction to trap yourself on the wall. Recheck F2 and D1 before continuing or passing.

Only a pass to the same half-wall spot
Shooting without checking the changed pressure

before.explanation: A changed blocker can make a shot more plausible. Control, pressure and the goalie still matter.

after.prompt: Before choosing between a pass and a shot, which direct line has more space from D1 in this view?

options.text: The line from the puck to F2
The line from the puck to the net

after.explanation: The line to F2 goes farther around D1 than the direct line to the net. That makes the half-wall pass worth assessing, not automatically the best play. The goalie, puck control and any change in pressure still matter; a later shot may become useful.
